items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: Then I made so many records with Roy, 'Braggin' In Brass,' all those things.

ctx.x: You mentioned Roy Eldridge. Let's talk about him for a while.

Roy, we made all his records with Billie Holiday together. Roy, Benny Goodman, Ben, Teddy Wilson, Kirby. We made the first records, 'Miss Brown to You,' 'What a Little Moonlight Can Do.' Roy was on those. Then I made so many records with Roy, 'Braggin' In Brass,' all those things. Roy, Charlie Shavers, Joe Thomas.

items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: It was Cozy Cole, John Kirby, Teddy Wilson, Chu Berry and myself.

ctx.x: No, I didn't run into Art Tatum until I was with McKinney's Cotton Pickers. I ran into him in 1933 or '34. Then we did a lot of playing together.

But I had been to New York, see. I was in New York, and I worked with Cecil Scott first at the Les Maison(?), and from the Les Maison(?)... Did I go to the Savoy? Maybe I went to the Savoy. No, no, no. Dickie Wells got me the job down at Smalls with Elmder Snowden in '31. Then they let Snowden go, and Charlie Johnson came in, and they kept me. I was the only one he kept, you know.
